content: 1. National legislation and policies should be reviewed and improved to ensure a balance between preventing the misuse, diversion, and trafficking of controlled substances and providing appropriate access to controlled medicines. This should align with the United Nations international drug control conventions. 2. Efforts should be made to explore ways to increase the availability and accessibility of medicines used in palliative care. This should involve consultations with Member States, relevant networks, civil society, and other international stakeholders, as appropriate. 3. Collaboration with the International Narcotics Control Board, the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime, health ministries, and other relevant authorities is essential to promote the availability and balanced control of controlled medicines for pain and symptom management. 4. Further cooperation with the International Narcotics Control Board is necessary to support Member States in establishing accurate estimates for enabling the availability of medicines for pain relief and palliative care. This includes better implementation of the guidance on estimating requirements for substances under international control. 5. Partnerships with UNICEF and other relevant organizations should be strengthened to promote and implement palliative care specifically for children. 6. The global situation of palliative care should be monitored, and progress in various initiatives and programs should be evaluated in collaboration with Member States and international partners. 7. Member States should be encouraged to provide adequate funding and improve cooperation for palliative care programs and research initiatives, particularly in resource-poor countries. This should align with the Programme budget 2014–2015, which addresses palliative care. 8. Research on effective models of palliative care in lowand middle-income countries should be encouraged, taking into account good practices. 9. A report on the progress in implementing this resolution should be presented to the Sixty-ninth World Health Assembly in 2016. 10. The International Narcotics Control Board and the World Health Organization have provided a guide on estimating requirements for substances under international control, published in New York by the United Nations in 2012.
